title: Echinacoside ameliorates post-stroke depression by activating BDNF signaling through modulation of Nrf2 acetylation.
authors: Yang, Zhou; Zhao, Yalin; Wang, Yanling; Liu, Xiaoli; Jiang, Yongxia; Jiang, Yongqu; Liu, Tingyu; Hu, Yue; Chang, Hui
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药成分松果菊苷通过Nrf2乙酰化激活BDNF信号改善卒中后抑郁，虽含分子对接但核心为湿实验与疾病机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-stroke depression (PSD) affects approximately one-third of stroke survivors, leading to adverse outcomes in rehabilitation, reduced quality of life, and increased mortality rates. Despite these implications, the underlying causes of PSD remain unclear, posing challenges for prevention and treatment. Echinacoside (ECH), a natural compound with known neuroprotective and antidepressant properties, holds significant therapeutic potential for PSD. However, the precise mechanism of its action remains unknown. PURPOSE: To unravel the specific mechanism through which ECH alleviates PSD by exploring the intricate interplay between ECH and Nrf2, as well as its impact on the BDNF/TrkB signaling axis. STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: A rat PSD model was established though middle cerebral artery occlusion coupled with chronic unpredictable mild stress, followed by ECH treatment. The rats' depressive state was evaluated using the sucrose preference test and force swimming test. Brain damage was assessed through TTC staining, Nissl staining, and TUNEL assay. The multifaceted mechanism of ECH in PSD was investigated using immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, RT-qPCR, dual-luciferase assay, and western blotting. Additionally, the interaction between ECH and Nrf2 was explored through molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis. RESULTS: Our findings unveiled a novel facet of ECH action, demonstrating its unique ability to upregulate Nrf2 through acetylation within the hippocampus of PSD-affected rats (p < 0.05). Moreover, ECH showcased its distinctive potential by enhancing BDNF transcriptional activity, activating the BDNF/TrkB signaling axis, and orchestrating a comprehensive response against oxidative stress and apoptosis, thereby alleviating PSD symptoms in rats (p < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: This study not only provides insights into the pivotal role of Nrf2 in mediating the BDNF/TrkB axis activation by ECH but also highlights the novelty of ECH's mechanism in addressing PSD. The elucidation of these unique aspects positions ECH as a groundbreaking candidate for further exploration and development in the realm of PSD intervention.
abstract_zh: 背景：卒中后抑郁（PSD）影响约三分之一的卒中幸存者，导致康复不良结局、生活质量下降及死亡率增加。尽管存在这些影响，PSD的潜在病因仍不明确，给预防和治疗带来挑战。松果菊苷（ECH）作为一种具有已知神经保护和抗抑郁特性的天然化合物，对PSD具有显著的治疗潜力。然而，其确切作用机制仍未知。目的：通过探讨ECH与Nrf2之间的复杂相互作用及其对BDNF/TrkB信号轴的影响，揭示ECH缓解PSD的具体机制。研究设计与方法：通过大脑中动脉闭塞联合慢性不可预见性轻度应激建立大鼠PSD模型，随后进行ECH治疗。采用蔗糖偏好实验和强迫游泳实验评估大鼠的抑郁状态。通过TTC染色、尼氏染色和TUNEL实验评估脑损伤。利用免疫荧光、免疫组织化学、RT-qPCR、双荧光素酶实验和蛋白质印迹法研究ECH在PSD中的多层面机制。此外，通过分子对接和微量热泳动技术探讨ECH与Nrf2之间的相互作用。结果：我们的发现揭示了ECH作用的新层面，证明其在PSD大鼠海马中通过乙酰化上调Nrf2的独特能力（p < 0.05）。此外，ECH通过增强BDNF转录活性、激活BDNF/TrkB信号轴，并协调针对氧化应激和凋亡的综合反应，从而缓解大鼠PSD症状，展示了其独特潜力（p < 0.05）。结论：本研究不仅提供了Nrf2在介导ECH激活BDNF/TrkB轴中关键作用的见解，还强调了ECH在应对PSD中机制的新颖性。这些独特方面的阐明使ECH成为PSD干预领域进一步探索和开发的突破性候选药物。
